name: Parti des Travailleurs
role: Left-wing political party in Algeria
notes: Left-wing Algerian political party (حزب العمال / PT) led by Louisa Hanoune; tabled recurring parliamentary amendments across successive Finance Bills to establish a progressive net wealth tax (Impôt sur la fortune) and opposed the 2017 deletion of the ISF.

name: Louisa Hanoune
role: Secrétaire générale du Parti des Travailleurs; former Députée à l'Assemblée Populaire Nationale
notes: Secretary General of the Workers' Party (Parti des Travailleurs / لويزة حنون) and former Member of the People's National Assembly for Algiers; longtime champion of a progressive net wealth tax and vocal critic of the parliamentary removal of the ISF in November 2017.

name: Ramdane Taazibt
role: Former Député à l'Assemblée Populaire Nationale for Alger (Parti des Travailleurs)
notes: Former Member of the People's National Assembly for Algiers (2007–2021) and senior leader of the Workers' Party (رمضان تعزيبت); repeatedly called for replacing austerity measures with a wealth tax and denounced the APN Finance Committee's suppression of the ISF in PLF 2018.

name: Smaïl Kouadria
role: Former Député à l'Assemblée Populaire Nationale for Annaba (Parti des Travailleurs); trade unionist
notes: Former Workers' Party Member of the People's National Assembly for Annaba and steelworkers' trade unionist (إسماعيل قوادرية); formally sponsored a parliamentary amendment to the 2014 Finance Bill to introduce a wealth tax, arguing the existing 1993 property tax was merely ink on paper.

name: Front des Forces Socialistes
role: Social-democratic political party in Algeria
notes: Social-democratic political party (جبهة القوى الاشتراكية / FFS) with representation in the Council of the Nation; protested the removal of the wealth tax in the 2018 Finance Bill and made the effective enforcement and municipal decentralization of the wealth tax a pillar of its 2024 presidential programme 'Vision pour demain'.

name: Youcef Aouchiche
role: Premier secrétaire national du Front des Forces Socialistes; Membre du Conseil de la Nation for Tizi Ouzou
notes: First National Secretary of the Socialist Forces Front (FFS / يوسف أوشيش), Member of the Council of the Nation for Tizi Ouzou (since 2022), former President of the APW of Tizi Ouzou (2017–2022), and 2024 presidential candidate; pledged in his platform 'Vision pour demain' to enforce a comprehensive individual net wealth tax and decentralize its management to municipalities (APCs).

name: Mouvement de la Société pour la Paix
role: Parliamentary political party in Algeria (Assemblée Populaire Nationale and Conseil de la Nation)
affiliation: Mouvement de la Société pour la Paix (MSP)
party: Mouvement de la Société pour la Paix
notes: Major parliamentary opposition party (حركة مجتمع السلم / حمس / MSP, holding 65 seats in the APN and 4 in the Council of the Nation); its leadership and parliamentary group opposed the removal of the wealth tax in PLF 2018 and advocated taxing large fortunes rather than low-income citizens.

name: Abdelmadjid Menasra
role: Former Président du Mouvement de la Société pour la Paix; former Ministre and Député
affiliation: Mouvement de la Société pour la Paix (MSP)
party: Mouvement de la Société pour la Paix
notes: Former President of the Movement of Society for Peace (MSP / عبد المجيد مناصرة), former Minister of Industry, and former Member of the People's National Assembly; condemned the parliamentary deletion of the 2018 wealth tax as a clear alignment against the poor.

name: Nacer Hamdadouche
role: Former Président du groupe parlementaire du MSP; former Député à l'Assemblée Populaire Nationale for Jijel
affiliation: Mouvement de la Société pour la Paix (MSP)
party: Mouvement de la Société pour la Paix
notes: Former President of the MSP Parliamentary Group and Member of the People's National Assembly for Jijel (ناصر حمدادوش); challenged the APN Finance Committee for rejecting opposition social amendments while withdrawing the wealth tax targeting the rich.

name: Lakhdar Benkhellaf
role: Former Président du groupe parlementaire de l'Union Ennahda-Adala-Bina; former Député for Constantine
affiliation: Front de la Justice et du Développement (FJD)
party: Front de la Justice et du Développement
notes: Former Member of the People's National Assembly for Constantine and parliamentary group leader for the Justice and Development Front (جبهة العدالة والتنمية / لخضر بن خلاف); repeatedly demanded the enforcement of a percentage-based net wealth tax so that wealthy Algerians share the burden of austerity.

name: Tahar Habchi
role: Former Député à l'Assemblée Populaire Nationale for Alger (Mouvement Ennahda)
notes: Senior leader of the Ennahda Movement and former Member of the People's National Assembly for Algiers (الطاهر حبشي); denounced the pressure exerted by 130 businessman-MPs in the ruling coalition to cancel the wealth tax in the 2018 Finance Bill.

name: Union Générale des Travailleurs Algériens
role: National trade union confederation of Algeria
notes: Algeria's principal national trade union confederation (الاتحاد العام للعمال الجزائريين / UGTA); formally demanded a reduction in personal income tax on wage earners (IRG) alongside the establishment of a wealth tax (taxe sur la fortune) for equitable tax distribution.

name: Salim Labatcha
role: Former Secrétaire général de l'Union Générale des Travailleurs Algériens (2019–2023); former Député for Alger
notes: Secretary General of the General Union of Algerian Workers (UGTA / سليم لباطشة) from 2019 to 2023 and former Workers' Party MP for Algiers; publicly called in October 2019 for instituting taxes on wealth to distribute the fiscal burden fairly and relieve salaried workers.

name: Abdelmadjid Tebboune
role: Président de la République Algérienne Démocratique et Populaire
notes: President of Algeria since December 2019 (عبد المجيد تبون); enacted the modern Impôt sur la fortune (ISF) in the 2020 Supplementary Finance Law and repeatedly directed the Council of Ministers in 2021 and 2022 to redefine and enforce the wealth tax and digitize property records rather than taxing only low-income workers.

name: Ahmed Ouyahia
role: Former Premier ministre d'Algérie; former Secrétaire général du Rassemblement National Démocratique
notes: Former Prime Minister of Algeria (أحمد أويحيى); introduced the government's landmark 2018 Finance Bill proposal for a progressive annual net wealth tax (1% to 3.5% on net assets above 50M DZD) before it was struck down by the APN Finance Committee.

name: Abderrahmane Raouya
role: Former Ministre des Finances d'Algérie (2017–2019, 2020, 2022)
notes: Former Minister of Finance (عبد الرحمان راوية); presented and defended the progressive net wealth tax in the 2018 Finance Bill (1%–3.5% above 50M DZD) and subsequently piloted the enactment of the revamped Impôt sur la fortune (0.15%–1% above 100M DZD) in the 2020 Supplementary Finance Law.

name: Laaziz Faid
role: Former Ministre des Finances d'Algérie (2023–2025)
notes: Former Minister of Finance (لعزيز فايد, March 2023 – February 2025); ordered the General Directorate of Taxes (DGI) to make 2023 the year of the wealth tax (Impôt sur la fortune) and deployed the CAD-Fisc cadastral database linking DGDN and DGI to expand the wealth tax base.

name: Gouvernement Algérien (Ministère des Finances)
role: National Ministry of Finance and Executive of Algeria
notes: National executive and Ministry of Finance (وزارة المالية); introduced the 2018 ISF bill, enacted the progressive Impôt sur la fortune in the 2020 Supplementary Finance Law, and introduced the 2026/2027 Finance Bill reform lowering the net wealth tax threshold from 100M DZD to 80M DZD with a 0.20%–1% progressive schedule.

name: Commission des Finances et du Budget de l'Assemblée Populaire Nationale
role: Standing Finance and Budget Committee of the lower house of Parliament
notes: Standing Finance and Budget Committee of the People's National Assembly (لجنة المالية والميزانية بالمجلس الشعبي الوطني); while its 8th-legislature majority blocked the ISF in 2017–2018, its 9th-legislature committee endorsed and refined the lowering of the wealth tax threshold from 100M DZD to 80M DZD (8 billion centimes) in 2025–2026.

name: Bouziane Mahmah
role: Professor of Economics and energy policy expert
notes: Algerian economics professor and analyst (بوزيان مهماه); argues for a fair, transparent, and enforceable wealth tax grounded in horizontal fiscal equity between salaried taxpayers and wealthy asset holders.

name: Aboubakr Sellami
role: Public finance and tax consultant (Expert en finances et fiscalité)
notes: Algerian tax and public finance specialist (أبوبكر سلامي); supports effective enforcement and tax-audit oversight of the wealth tax (Impôt sur la fortune) while recommending calibrating the exemption threshold to 200M–300M DZD to account for urban primary residence values.

name: Mouvement El Bina
role: Parliamentary political party in Algeria (Assemblée Populaire Nationale and Conseil de la Nation)
notes: Major parliamentary political party (حركة البناء الوطني / Mouvement El Bina, holding 39 seats in the People's National Assembly); its presidential platform and parliamentary group advocated expanding the tax base and enforcing collection of the net wealth tax (الضريبة على الثروة) alongside tax relief for wage earners.

name: Abdelkader Bengrina
role: Président du Mouvement El Bina; former Ministre du Tourisme and former Membre du Conseil Consultatif National
notes: President of the National Construction Movement (حركة البناء الوطني / عبد القادر بن قرينة), former Minister of Tourism, and 2019 presidential candidate (runner-up); pledged in his 2019 presidential election platform to broaden the tax base and enforce collection of the wealth tax (الضريبة على الثروة).

name: Parti Socialiste des Travailleurs
role: Left-wing political party in Algeria
notes: Algerian anti-capitalist left-wing political party (حزب العمال الاشتراكي / PST, founded 1989); campaigned for taxing large fortunes and condemned the government and Parliament in December 2017 for burying the Impôt sur la fortune while granting tax amnesties to wealthy informal-sector barons.

name: Conseil des Lycées d'Algérie
role: Autonomous secondary-school teachers' trade union and member of the Intersyndicale
notes: Autonomous Algerian secondary-school teachers' union (مجلس ثانويات الجزائر / CLA) and founding member of the Autonomous Unions' Intersyndicale; formally denounced the APN Finance Committee's cancellation of the Impôt sur la fortune in November 2017, stating the wealth tax would have had highly positive effects on reducing the budget deficit.

name: Djelloul Djoudi
role: Former Président du groupe parlementaire du Parti des Travailleurs à l'Assemblée Populaire Nationale
notes: Senior leader of the Workers' Party (جلول جودي) and former Chief of the PT Parliamentary Group in the People's National Assembly; formally proposed during the September 2017 Government Action Plan debate that the executive enact a genuine and equitable fiscal reform instituting an Impôt sur la fortune.

name: Nadia Chouitem
role: Former Députée à l'Assemblée Populaire Nationale for Alger (Parti des Travailleurs)
notes: Former Workers' Party Member of the People's National Assembly for Algiers and Political Bureau member (نادية شويتم); led parliamentary floor protests alongside Ramdane Taazibt in November 2017 against the suppression of Article 12 (Impôt sur la fortune) in the 2018 Finance Bill.

name: Hakim Berri
role: Former Député à l'Assemblée Populaire Nationale for Batna (Rassemblement National Démocratique)
notes: Former RND Member of the People's National Assembly for Batna (حكيم بري, 2017–2021); broke ranks during the June 2018 Supplementary Finance Bill debate to declare it illogical that the Impôt sur la fortune proposal was rejected in PLF 2018 while VAT exemptions were removed on ordinary citizens.

name: Aïmene Benabderrahmane
role: Former Premier ministre d'Algérie (2021–2023) and Ministre des Finances (2020–2022)
notes: Former Prime Minister of Algeria (2021–2023), Minister of Finance (2020–2022), and Governor of the Bank of Algeria (أيمن بن عبد الرحمان); directed the tax administration to establish a national registry (بطاقية) of individuals subject to the Impôt sur la fortune following the LFC 2020 progressive wealth tax reform.

name: Brahim Djamel Kassali
role: Former Ministre des Finances d'Algérie (2022–2023)
notes: Former Minister of Finance of Algeria (إبراهيم جمال كسالي, 2022–2023); piloted the 2023 Finance Bill extending tax audit powers to the Impôt sur la fortune for natural persons holding assets inside and outside Algeria.

name: Abdelkrim Bouzred
role: Former Ministre des Finances d'Algérie (2025–2026)
notes: Minister of Finance of Algeria since February 2025 (عبد الكريم بوزرد) and former Secretary General of the Ministry of Finance; presented the 2026 Finance Bill before the People's National Assembly revising the Impôt sur la fortune threshold from 100M DZD to 80M DZD and clarifying its enforcement mechanisms.

name: Kamel Rezig
role: Professor of Economics at University of Blida; Ministre du Commerce
notes: Professor of Economics and Public Finance at the University of Blida and Minister of Trade (كمال رزيق); publicly endorsed the introduction of the wealth tax in November 2017 and condemned the APN Finance Committee's deletion of the tax as a 'crime against the people', proposing a 0.5%–1.5% rate schedule above 200M DZD.

name: Houari Tigharsi
role: Lecturer at the Faculty of Economics, University of Algiers; former Député à l'Assemblée Populaire Nationale
notes: Economist, Lecturer at the Faculty of Economics at the University of Algiers, and former Member of the APN Finance and Budget Committee (هواري تيغرسي); endorsed the 2026/2027 Finance Bill reform lowering the net wealth tax threshold from 100M DZD to 80M DZD as a measure that broadens the tax base and strengthens fiscal justice.

name: Abdellatif Rebah
role: Algerian economist and development researcher
notes: Algerian economist and author (عبد اللطيف رباح); advocated taxing large fortunes and patrimonies rather than cutting universal social subsidies, criticizing Algeria's tax system as overly lenient toward wealth holders.

name: Mohamed Chérif Belmihoub
role: Professor of Economics and Public Management at École Nationale d'Administration (ENA Algiers); former Ministre délégué
notes: Professor of Economics at the National School of Administration (ENA Algiers) and former Minister Delegate for Prospective and Statistics (محمد شريف بلميهوب, 2020–2021); argued during the 2017 budget debates that improving the yield and enforcement of the existing net wealth tax (impôt sur le patrimoine) on personal assets was preferable to improvised tax measures.

name: Hamza Boughadi
role: Economic consultant and financial analyst
notes: Algerian economic consultant and analyst (حمزة بوغادي); argued in November 2022 that Algeria can and should enforce the wealth tax (الضريبة على الثروة) in parallel with targeted social subsidy reform and economic data modernization.

name: Mohammed Lamine Lebbou
role: Ministre des Finances d'Algérie (since September 2026); former Gouverneur de la Banque d'Algérie
notes: Minister of Finance of Algeria since September 2026 and former Governor of the Bank of Algeria (محمد لمين لبو); presented the 2027 Finance Bill (PLF 2027, Article 25) lowering the Impôt sur la fortune threshold from 100M DZD to 80M DZD, revising the progressive rate schedule (0.20% to 1% above 400M DZD), and introducing 10%–25% late-filing penalties and taxation d'office.

name: Kamel Aissani
role: Former Directeur général des Impôts (2019–2020)
notes: Senior tax administrator and Director General of Taxes from April 2019 to February 2020 (كمال عيساني); defended the restructuring of the property/wealth tax (Article 26 of the 2020 Finance Bill) before the APN Finance and Budget Committee in October 2019 as the start of a gradual reform of the tax system.

name: Mourad Goumiri
role: Professeur des universités and financial expert
notes: Algerian university professor and Doctor of State in Economics (مراد قويري); argued on Radio M during the October 2017 budget debate that Algeria should have instituted an Impôt sur la fortune long ago alongside property and revaluation taxes so that wealthy individuals contribute to tax revenues.

name: Noureddine Bouderba
role: Trade unionist, social protection expert, and former social affairs adviser to the UGTA
notes: Veteran Algerian trade unionist, social security specialist, and former UGTA social affairs adviser (نور الدين بودربة); repeatedly condemned the non-taxation of large fortunes and patrimonies and called for instituting the Impôt sur la fortune and making the patrimony tax effective.

name: Finabi Conseil
role: Financial and tax policy research and consulting cabinet in Algiers
notes: Algiers-based financial and tax policy research cabinet founded by Chabane Assad; published the landmark January 2023 policy study 'Impôt sur la fortune : Une niche fiscale négligée' demonstrating that at most 67 taxpayers paid the Algerian wealth tax in 2022 and calling for structural enforcement.

name: Chabane Assad
role: Fondateur et directeur du cabinet Finabi Conseil; financial and tax expert
notes: Financial and tax expert, member of the National Economic, Social and Environmental Council (CNESE), and founder of Finabi Conseil (شعبان أسعد); authored the 2023 study 'Impôt sur la fortune : Une niche fiscale négligée' characterizing the wealth tax as a neglected tax niche with exponential revenue potential.

name: Ahmed Sahlia
role: University economics professor and financial expert
affiliation: Université Mohamed Chérif Messaadia de Souk Ahras
notes: Algerian economics professor and financial expert (أحمد سواهلية); criticized the historical non-application of taxes to businessmen and wealthy individuals and endorsed the 2020 activation and digitized enforcement of the wealth tax (الضريبة على الثروة).
